title: Review of c04's crawler forks: on fresh seed 3 the actin cut stops crawling and division (speed 0.032 vs 0.139, 0 vs 4 later splits) and starvation leaves 11 'undead' round bodies, as reported
summary: Looked at rim_cut/sheet.png, post.txt and starve/seed1/sheet.png, then ran the finding's world.py on fresh seed 3 three ways (labkit, 240 frames, T=600): uncut, actin production cut to 0.2x at t=300 (w_cut.py) and all food removed at t=300 (w_starve.py), and measured them with the finding's tools/post.py after frame 120 (post.txt). Uncut: mean body speed 0.139 (90th pct 0.40), 4 persistent splits after the fork, 15 bodies at t=600. Cut: 0.032 (0.06), 0 splits, 12 bodies, and the sheet shows the crescents rounding up at the fork. Starved: 0.021 (0.03), 0 splits, 11 small round bodies that persist unchanged to t=600 (rerun_starve/seed3/sheet.png t=337-600), so the negative result (no L4c: cells do not die when starved) replicates too. Not re-run: dt/2.

observations.B: post.txt: actin cut at t=300 drops mean speed 0.139 -> 0.032 and later splits 4 -> 0 on seed 3; rerun_cut/seed3/sheet.png cells round up after t=300; rerun_starve/seed3/sheet.png: 11 bodies persist to t=600 without food

controls_run.B: rerun_uncut/seed3: the same seed without the fork

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed per fork; the uncut and cut runs are separate runs of the same seed (identical up to t=300), so the comparison is a branched twin only up to the run's determinism.
